Round 19 — the home page's date, and how loudly it says where it came from

The operator's word was that the date on the home page does not read as maintained data. Three rulings make "dynamic" a claim this tree cannot make rather than one it declines: the schedule is a derived snapshot nobody fetches at request time (D73), every route is prerendered (design/README.md), and the motion tiers stop at 250ms with no pulse (D115, MS35's check:reduced-motion). What the page can honestly carry is the register it already runs — the feed's own read date, in D322's wording (D232's stamp). So this round prices WHERE that line sits and HOW LOUD the date is, in the two vocabularies the design system owns.

Every row is a byte delta on the shipped page, photographed by the same Firefox load that produced its numbers, after the ratified faces settled. The screenshot is firefox's own and is taken at load, so it is the layout proof rather than a font proof (page-measure.mjs's note). Baseline row: A — the date as it stands (the baseline) — the shipped page with this item’s register line removed. The photographs are the built page and carry the built sheet; this specimen page's own type and spacing are specimen-only — it loads no site CSS, so read colour and measure layout off the shots, not off the rows of prose beneath them. Every number on this page is a reading of `design/grill/round19/report.json` — written by `npm run round19` at 2026-11-19T07:10:50.502Z, re-rendered by `node design/grill/round19-build.mjs`; the record is the truth and this page is generated from it. The page height is load-to-load noise, not a variant's cost: the shipped baseline's identical bytes came in 4341px and 4402px in one run, a 61px spread at 320, so a page-height delta under that spread is no evidence of anything — the number that prices a variant is the block's own box, in the column beside it.

Token arithmetic against the same oracle the contrast gate uses; check:contrast asserts pairs and does not adjudicate which one a date takes, so a colour row is the operator’s to choose. The tint ground against paper is a layer pair, not a text pair: its own bar is BARS.layer.

The nav's date chip, and the row it has to fit

@1240 the outer row's box is 1164×40 at x=32, its ink reaches 315px over 1 line(s) — holds one line of links with 881px of room left in the box the page gives it; @390 the outer row's box is 346×40 at x=16, its ink reaches 299px over 1 line(s) — holds one line of links with 63px of room left in the box the page gives it; @320 the outer row's box is 276×40 at x=16, its ink reaches 299px over 1 line(s) — runs 7px past the box the page gives it, and the row ships nowrap — so an overflowing label set is a failed width probe, not a silent re-wrap. D311’s number for this element is history; the row above is what this load measured. The chip is not hidden above 380 either way: the built sheet ships "@media (width>=380px){.xs\:inline{display:inline}}" against --breakpoint-xs: 380px (src/styles/global.css:48), so what the chip column can change is the 320 floor and nothing above it. The row measured here is the flex row walked up from the Dates link, not the max-width wrapper the page's

element is.

How to read the table

  • the boxes are the page's own layout after the ratified faces settle (date-fresh-measure.js); the shot is firefox's at load
  • the hero block's OWN box is the quoted delta: the page height repeats across loads of identical bytes (the shipped page came in 3925 and 3985 in one run), so pageHeights prints every sample and pageSpread prints the gap, and a page-height delta of less than that spread is no evidence of anything
  • contrasts are token arithmetic against the same oracle the contrast gate uses; BARS.text is the ratified text bar
  • the nav’s date chip is NOT hidden above 380: the built sheet ships `@media (width>=380px){.xs\:inline{display:inline}}` (the breakpoint is --breakpoint-xs, src/styles/global.css:48), so the shipped chip already paints at 390 and 1240 and only the 320 floor is in question — the chip column proves that, it is not a claim
  • the stamp line is the sentence /dates prints, verbatim: D322 rules one wording for one provenance fact, and check-content.mjs pairs surfaces WITHIN a page, so this repeat is not a cross-page pair it can see
